laura: Heads-up — ACME committed to an annual reserved plan. Need a quick preflight: throughput sizing, reserved GPU recommendation, autoscale policy, and answers for a security questionnaire. Customer expectation: sustained baseline ~200 RPS, 400 RPS 10-min bursts, ~1.2M tokens/day. Mix is ~70% chat, 30% embeddings. Can SE + Ops + Security sync?

michael_se: I can take lead on SE side. Couple quick q's: avg tokens per chat request? percent of sync vs async calls? embedding QPS shape?

laura: avg chat ~220 tokens/request, embeddings are 1-2k vector per request but small token count. Traffic is spiky around US business hours, 4:00–6:00pm UTC for 10–20 mins. They'll want <200ms p50 gen latency for short prompts.

raj_ops: Based on that shape, proposal: reserved pool = 4 x A100-type GPUs for baseline, autoscale up to 12 GPUs for burst headroom. Use burst credits and prewarm windows during that 4–6pm UTC window. Recommend continuous batching window = 20–30ms, max batch size cap per model, and KV cache warmup on preheat.

michael_se: Sounds reasonable. To check: are we assuming the chat model is quantized 4-bit? That impacts GPU throughput drastically. Also, what embedding model — on-device smaller model or larger?

raj_ops: Assume they take our quantized variant (recommended) for chat. For embeddings plan on 1x smaller instance class — embeddings are CPU-friendly but still benefit from GPU for lower latency. Cost/throughput numbers we can sketch: baseline 4 GPUs covers ~250 RPS for chat when quantized; with embeddings mixed traffic we'd still be fine. Autoscale triggers: CPU token rate + queue depth + p95 latency. I suggest: scale-up when queue_depth > 40 or p95 > 400ms for 2 consecutive 30s windows. Scale-down after 5m stable below thresholds.

eve_security: Security notes: customer needs KMS integration (bring-your-own-key), VPC peering or private link, and per-request audit logging retained 1y. Need to confirm SOC2/ISO artifacts — product security can provide. Also they asked about model weights provenance and whether we retain any customer prompt text outside logs. We must confirm retention policy and redaction options.

laura: They also asked how reserved capacity affects pricing vs usage-based. Can you sketch numbers I can hand to finance?

michael_se: Quick sketch (ballpark, needs finance review): reserved cap fee = $X/month per GPU (committed) plus a reduced per-token usage fee; burst credits priced separately. Example: 4 reserved GPUs -> $Y/month commit -> effective token price ~0.6x on steady usage compared to pure on-demand. I'll put exact ranges in a follow-up doc.

raj_ops: Operational checklist for POC/handoff: 1) schedule KV warmup job 30m before peak; 2) preheat reserved pool during the agreed window; 3) enable prefix caching for common prompts; 4) deploy autoscale policy with the thresholds above; 5) set graceful degradation to fallback model (smaller) at p99 > 2s. I'll paste an example autoscale snippet: 

raj_ops: ```
policy: autoscale
min_replicas: 4
max_replicas: 12
scale_up: when queue_depth > 40 or p95_latency_ms > 400 for 30s
scale_down: when p95_latency_ms < 300 and queue_depth < 10 for 5m
preheat: schedule 30m before peak
```

laura: Perfect. Can we answer the security questionnaire items about data residency and retention today? They need a written statement for the sales deck.

eve_security: We can provide: 1) We support region pinning and private deployments (VPC). 2) KMS integration for customer-managed keys (BYOK). 3) Audit logs exportable to their SIEM (S3/ELK). 4) Default retention 30d for full request logs, with options to extend to 1y for enterprise. Note: for any on-prem install we can support longer retention and air-gapped options. I'll attach SOC2/ISO certs in the doc.

michael_se: I'll capture the capacity assumptions and the pricing sketch into a single one-pager and tag finance. Laura — want me to draft the POC runbook for customer signoff?

laura: Yes please. Include preheat schedule, KV warmup script, observability checks (tail p95/p99, model fallback events), and the security checklist. Also include a clear escalation path.

raj_ops: I'll provision a test harness to simulate their spike (400 RPS for 10m) so we can validate autoscale behavior. Schedule: I can run smoke test tomorrow 09:00 UTC if that works.

laura: Tomorrow 09:00 UTC works. michael_se please cc finance and prod-security on the one-pager.

deploy-bot: Scheduled: capacity-smoke-test for thread 2222223333 — started at 2222228233, estimated runtime 12m. Logs will be posted to #eng-sre after completion.

laura: Awesome — thanks all. Post-test let's regroup for a 30-min signoff call. :thumbsup:

michael_se: Got it, will draft doc today. :+1:

raj_ops: I'll monitor the smoke test and share results.

eve_security: I'll compile the security artifacts and drop into the shared folder.

laura: Closing the loop — after the smoke test we'll finalize the reservation count and pricing for the contract.
